entities.summary:
Francesco Condulmer was a cardinal of the Roman Catholic Church, born in unknown year and died on November 8, 1453. He played a significant role in the papal conclave that led to the election of Pope Nicholas V, who later initiated the Renaissance era through his patronage of artists and intellectuals.

As a key figure in the papal court during the late 15th century, Condulmer contributed to the reform efforts aimed at restoring the Church's authority after the Western Schism. He was part of a group of cardinals who met in Pisa in 1459 to discuss reforms and elect a new pope.

Condulmer's legacy is also tied to his association with the Renaissance humanist movement, which emphasized classical learning and individualism. His support for artists like Michelangelo and Raphael helped shape the artistic landscape of Italy during this period.

In the end, Condulmer's influence on the papacy and art world was lasting, as he helped pave the way for a new era of creativity and intellectual curiosity that would have far-reaching consequences for Western culture.
